newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada pledges funds to save CBC's foreign radio arm.
newsitem.headline: Canada pledges funds to save CBC's foreign radio arm.

text.p: Radio Canada International, Canada's voice to the world which was slated to close next March, will get funding to survive for another year at least, the federal government said on Thursday.
RCI's parent, the Canadian Broadcasting Corp., said last week that the international radio operation would have to close due to a lack of funding.
The cash-strapped CBC, Canada's public broadcaster, is currently trimming services and cutting jobs to deal with a C$414 million reduction in government subsidies.
But the federal government said on Thursday that RCI's C$16 million in funding will be part of a new foreign communications strategy.

"We certainly recognise how important it is to have an effective voice for Canada abroad to promote trade and development," Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy told the House of Commons in Canada's Parliament.
RCI's 125 employees provide shortwave and satellite service broadcasts in seven languages to listeners overseas.
